clue.text: Welshman's raised floor

wordplay.note: Dai is the stock Welsh man's name in crosswords, and the possessive adds the final S

explanation.surface: A Welshman shows off the raised floor he owns.
explanation.walkthrough: DAI is a common Welsh short form of David; DAI'S, with the apostrophe dropped, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A platform at one end of a hall, raised above the rest, is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: Fool declines credit

parts.note: dips means declines, as prices do
tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A fool turns down the offer of credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a rod for measuring oil, it is also British slang for an idiot.

clue.text: Ancient British tribe somewhat artistic, enigmatic

indicators.note: somewhat means only partly, so just part of these words is used

parts.note: the tribe's name runs across the end of artistic and the start of enigmatic

explanation.surface: An ancient tribe is said to have been rather artistic and mysterious.
explanation.definitionFit: This tribe of eastern England, led by Boudicca, rose against Roman rule.

clue.text: Strained sweet courses knocked back

indicators.note: knocking something back turns it the other way, so the word for the sweet courses is read from the end

parts.note: the sweet courses at the end of a meal are desserts

explanation.surface: Someone eats the puddings too fast and feels the strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Strained and this word are synonyms for being under tension or pressure.

clue.text: Hat drunkard pinches quietly

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip tightly, so the drinker's word squeezes the soft letter inside it

parts.note: a toper is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A drunk quietly steals a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinches' reads as steals, but here it means holds tight. P is the music notation for piano, quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: A top hat, the tall formal kind, is commonly called this.

clue.text: A Manc goalie, awfully self-important

indicators.note: awfully means badly done, so the letters of A Manc goalie are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, these eleven letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A Manchester goalkeeper behaving with dreadful vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: A Manc is someone from Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsessed with oneself, thinking oneself very important; a near synonym of conceited.

clue.text: Singular language used by golf party

parts.note: Hindi is a major language of India
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A single language is spoken at a golf club party.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively, noisy celebration; informal word for a social gathering.

clue.text: Fight between two outstanding lawyers primarily

parts.note: a debt still outstanding is due

indicators.note: primarily means first, so only the opening letter of lawyers is used

parts.note: its first letter alone is used

explanation.surface: Two fine lawyers clash, at least at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' reads as excellent, but means still owed.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal combat between two people, traditionally with swords or pistols.

clue.text: Exercise before small drink

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
to sup is to drink, in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Do a little workout before a modest drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This floor exercise, pushing the body up with the arms, is a standard gym routine.

clue.text: One appearing in court in connection with a racket?

definitions.meaning: sounds like a defendant in a law court, but the court is a badminton court
a racket suggests a criminal scheme, but it is the bat that strikes this feathered object

explanation.surface: A crook turns up in court charged over some racket.
explanation.definitionFit: The feathered projectile of badminton is hit over the net with rackets on a court.

clue.text: Suppose old identification number unusable ultimately

parts.note: a PIN is a personal identification number

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the closing letter of unusable is wanted

parts.note: its last letter alone is used

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that an old PIN no longer works.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a view or think something likely; supposing and offering an opinion are near synonyms.

clue.text: Group of musical mimics curtailed trip, reportedly barred on Scottish isle

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another comes after it
a curtailed word has its tail cut off, so trip loses its last letter

parts.note: a trip, here a journey, loses its tail
Bute is an island in the Firth of Clyde

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word that sounds like the one given, here the word for barred

parts.note: barred means banned, which sounds like the word wanted

explanation.surface: A holiday cut short because someone was barred from a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a group copies a famous act's songs and look, so its members are imitators of other musicians.

clue.text: Choppy sea, for me, horrifying

indicators.note: choppy water is broken up, so these letters are broken up and reordered

parts.note: taken as written, these letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A rough sea is a frightening thing for the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightening in appearance or power; the two words are close synonyms.

clue.text: Key tip joining variable fabric

parts.note: C is a musical key
a tip is a piece of advice, a hint
Z is one of the letters used in algebra for a variable

explanation.surface: A pointer about the key fits together with a variable fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazed printed cotton, often floral, used for curtains and upholstery.

clue.text: Slope incorporated railway

parts.note: Inc is the abbreviation for incorporated, as in company names
a railway line

explanation.surface: A slope has been built into the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient up or down, a sloping stretch of ground.

clue.text: Jack and Nigel arranged short catchy tune

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: letters that are arranged are put in a new order, so Nigel's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name taken as written supplies the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Two people, Jack and Nigel, arrange a short tune together.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple catchy tune, especially one written for an advertisement.

clue.text: Whimsical old fashion designer embracing individual

indicators.note: embracing means holding in the arms, so the designer's name goes around the letter for one

parts.note: Mary Quant was the British designer of the 1960s known for the miniskirt
I is one, a single individual

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned designer hugging someone in a whimsical way.
explanation.definitionFit: Charmingly odd or old-fashioned, attractively unusual.

clue.text: Dark, cold agent, powerfully built, needing no introduction

parts.note: a rep, or representative, acts as an agent

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter, here removed

parts.note: powerfully built means muscular

explanation.surface: A shadowy, chilly agent with a strong physique who needs no introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer relates to twilight, so it describes dim, dusky light; dark is a fair loose synonym.

clue.text: Mark, during Christmas, served up fruit

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means read from bottom to top
the letter for mark comes during, so inside, the word for Christmas

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A mark served up fruit at Christmas time.
explanation.definitionFit: A sour yellow citrus fruit.

clue.text: Tasteless stuff supported by one French filmmaker

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece supported by another sits above it

parts.note: tat is cheap, tasteless goods
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Kitsch held up by one French director.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Tati was the French director and star of Monsieur Hulot's Holiday.

clue.text: Friend in the past touring Michigan

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the word for in the past goes around the state's abbreviation

parts.note: ago means in the past
MI is the US postal abbreviation for Michigan

explanation.surface: A friend once travelled round Michigan.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Spanish word for a pal, used informally in English too.

clue.text: Signior regularly holds arm up in the air

indicators.note: one part holds another by going around it
taking letters regularly means every other one, here the second, fourth and sixth of Signior

parts.note: the word taken as written, of which every second letter is kept
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: An Italian gentleman holds an arm raised high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up in the air' looks like it describes the arm, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe something undecided, left in a state of uncertainty.

clue.text: Move along slippery surface with girl following cones maybe

indicators.note: the girl's name comes after the frozen treats

parts.note: an ice cream cone is an example of an ice
Kate is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone glides along an icy surface after a girl, perhaps round traffic cones.
explanation.definitionFit: To glide over ice on bladed boots is to travel across a slippery surface.

clue.text: Eager, bringing forward new joint

indicators.note: the letter for new is moved up from the end of the word for eager to nearer the front

parts.note: keen means eager

explanation.surface: An eager person brings something new forward.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint between thigh and shin in the leg.
